key_facts: The Chair called the meeting to order and mentioned that today's proceedings will be televised.
Mr. Paul Manly presented a petition calling for a ban on cosmetic testing using animals in Canada, following the European Union model.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre tabled an e-petition regarding a tragic boating accident involving his constituent's son, Joshua, and called for amendments to small vessel regulations.
The Prime Minister stated that the government's priority was to get money out to Canadians quickly and that fraud is unacceptable with measures in place to detect it.
Hon. Andrew Scheer questioned the government about ignoring red flags of fraud and whether they would adjust programs to include more eligible businesses.
The Prime Minister responded that the government prioritized getting help to as many Canadians as possible quickly and would continue to tweak programs.
Hon. Yves-Franois Blanchet questioned the government about the timeline for employment incentives accompanying the Canada emergency response benefit.
The Prime Minister stated that students can apply for the Canada emergency student benefit starting Friday and will be directed to a job bank.
Hon. Jagmeet Singh raised concerns about the impact of the pandemic on seniors, noting that 80% or more of deaths were among seniors in long-term care homes.
The Prime Minister acknowledged the importance of respecting provincial jurisdiction but emphasized the federal government's role in supporting provinces.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked how many emergency response benefit cheques had been sent to people flagged as fraudulent.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that 7.7 million Canadians had received the Canada emergency response benefit.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre questioned the number of prisoners who had received the benefit, and Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos clarified that the benefit was an emergency measure.
The Auditor General reported that he was dropping half of his audits due to lack of funding, and Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government was increasing funding for the Auditor General.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked if the government would give the Auditor General the requested funding, and Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos affirmed that the government was supporting the Auditor General.
Hon. Grard Deltell questioned whether 200,000 people had fraudulently used emergency assistance, and Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos clarified that the numbers referred to legitimate recipients.
Hon. Tracy Gray raised concerns about small business owners not qualifying for CEBA due to not having a business account or being owner-operators.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the eligibility criteria for CEBA had been adjusted to include lower payroll thresholds.
Hon. John Barlow highlighted concerns about the agricultural sector and the potential loss of 15% of farms.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau mentioned that $77.5 million had been allocated for processors and $50 million for beef producers under the AgriRecovery program.
Hon. Michael Chong raised concerns about the leaking of labor force survey data and its impact on financial markets, and Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government would investigate the leak.

Hon. Yves-Franois Blanchet asked about the increase in health transfers to Quebec and the provinces, and Hon. Patty Hajdu stated that the government was working with provinces to support healthcare needs.
Hon. Marilne Gill questioned the government about specific assistance for seasonal industries like tourism and fishing.
Hon. Navdeep Bains mentioned that the government had implemented significant measures to support the tourism and seasonal industries.

Hon. Jagmeet Singh questioned the government about limiting CEO bonuses and share buybacks, and Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government was clear about not allowing share buybacks for large enterprises.
Hon. Bill Morneau mentioned that the government was not allowing companies convicted of tax evasion to access funds and was evaluating eligibility continuously.
Hon. Randy Hoback questioned the government about the approval of Canadian-made disinfectants and the support for farmers.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that Health Canada had accelerated the approval process for disinfectants.
Hon. Ben Lobb raised concerns about the carbon tax impacting pork farmers and the government's response.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government had introduced exemptions for agriculture in the carbon tax.
Hon. Larry Maguire questioned the government about the eligibility of businesses for wage subsidy programs and the ability to refinance loans.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the wage subsidy program had been amended to allow for a 15% revenue decline and that the government was considering refinancing options.
Hon. Tako Van Popta questioned the government about the wage subsidy program's applicability to high-growth and merged companies.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government was considering changes to accommodate these types of businesses.
Hon. Paul Manly questioned the government about allowing dividend income for CEBA eligibility.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government was working with businesses to find solutions.
Hon. Scott Duvall questioned the government about increasing OAS and GIS benefits for seniors and the omission of people with disabilities.
Hon. Deb Schulte stated that the government had provided one-time payments and additional supports for seniors.
Hon. Maxime Blanchette-Joncas questioned the effectiveness of the rent assistance program and the government's commitment to reviewing it.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the rent relief program was significant and more information would be available soon.
Hon. Greg McLean questioned the government about the design of the CECRA program and its benefits for landlords and tenants.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the program aimed to provide advantages for both parties and that details would be announced.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre questioned the total assets, liabilities, and equity of the Government of Canada.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government was in a strong fiscal position and focused on supporting Canadians.
